tips.title: Airbrushing Vallejo Model Air vs Model Color
tips.text: Vallejo Model Air is thinner than Model Color, requiring less thinning. Mix Model Air at a 3:1 paint to thinner ratio using Vallejo Airbrush Thinner. For Model Color, mix at a 1:1 ratio. Add 2-3 drops of Vallejo Flow Improver per 10 drops of thinned paint. Spray Model Air at 1.5-2.0 bar pressure, Model Color at 1.0-1.5 bar. Test consistency on a white plastic spoon.

tips.title: Base Coat Technique with Alclad II
tips.text: Alclad II offers excellent metal finish but requires proper preparation. Pre-shade panel lines with acrylic paint, then apply Alclad II using an HVLP gun or airbrush at 1.5-2.0 bar pressure. Allow to dry for 10 minutes, then buff off excess with a soft cloth. Apply a second coat, allowing 20 minutes' drying time between coats.

tips.title: Camouflage Masking with Eduard Masks
tips.text: Eduard masks simplify camouflage painting. Cut masks to size, trim edges if necessary. Apply with Eduard Masking Solvent, allowing 30 seconds' drying time before painting. Paint with Vallejo Model Air, allowing 24 hours' drying time before removing masks. Remove masks using tweezers and a sharp blade to lift edges.

tips.title: Applying AK Interactive Washes
tips.text: AK Interactive Washes add depth and realism. Shake bottle well before use. Dilute wash with AK Interactive Thinner at a 1:1 ratio for initial application. Apply with a flat brush, working wash into recesses and panel lines. Allow to dry 24 hours, then remove excess with a damp cloth. Apply a second coat undiluted for deeper effect.

tips.title: Chipping with Sponge Technique
tips.text: Sponge technique adds realistic chipping to edges. Use a natural sea sponge, cut into small pieces. Dip sponge in Vallejo Model Color or AMMO by Mig Jimenez enamel paint, matching desired chip color. Gently dab sponge onto model's edge, varying pressure for chip size. Allow paint to dry 15 minutes before sealing with varnish.
